Thanks for fixing this — the styling guide no longer sends readers to the wrong compiler setup.

What I verified:

- The corrected wording matches the app: "The repo ships no SWC example app: `apps/example-nextjs-stylex` compiles StyleX with the Babel plugin and PostCSS, so read it for the PostCSS layer setup, not for the transform." Its package, Babel, and PostCSS configuration show exactly that, and its Next config carries no SWC wiring.
- The change is now just that one-sentence correction — the drift test added in earlier commits has been dropped, and no governing requirement needs a bespoke test for a one-line prose fix, so nothing else is required on that front.
- I also checked whether any other place needs the same update: the getting-started guide lists this app only as "Next.js + StyleX" and the `example-nextjs-source` README only as "StyleX for product only", neither with an SWC claim, so no other place needs this correction.

One note for transparency: I could not run the full test suite or a browser locally in this review environment, so this is verified from the shipped prose, the example app's configuration, and a repo-wide search rather than a local test run.

Thanks for the contribution. This review is waiting on a maintainer decision before it can be approved.

The PR adds a new workflow that would publish packages to GitHub Packages whenever a GitHub release is created. Approval needs a maintainer to provide or identify the governing spec for that additional publishing path — what must be settled is the registry (GitHub Packages versus the public npm registry used today), the trigger (release creation), which packages it would publish, and the credential model. The existing release workflow describes itself as the single source of truth for npm publishing of the `@astryxdesign/*` packages to the public npm registry via trusted publishing, and no current spec I could find authorizes a second path.

The new devcontainer file is unrelated to that publishing change, so please remove it from this PR or split it into its own PR, where it can be considered with its own justification.

Independent of those decisions, a few things in the PR as written would need fixing:

- `vitest.config.ts` comments out the `node:path` import, but `path` is still used throughout the config, so the test config cannot load and the test suite fails before running.
- Both workflow jobs run `npm ci`, which needs a `package-lock.json`; this repository uses pnpm and has only `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so the jobs would fail at install.
- The publish step runs `npm publish` once at the repository root with no build step. The root package is private, and the publishable packages are the individual `@astryxdesign/*` packages, so this would not publish them.
- The workflow pins Node 20, while the repository keeps its Node version in `.nvmrc` (currently 24) as the single source of truth.
- The devcontainer file selects a generic image with no Node, pnpm, or install setup, so it does not set up this repository's toolchain.

If a maintainer confirms the GitHub Packages path should exist, rebuilding the workflow on the repository's existing pnpm setup and per-package publishing flow would address the workflow points above.

Thanks for a focused, well-evidenced change. Widening `DialogHeader`'s `title` and `subtitle` to `ReactNode`, keeping a link working in the subtitle, preserving focus-on-open and the dialog's accessible name, and handling a `0` subtitle cleanly all look sound, and string callers are unchanged.

Approval needs a maintainer decision first. No current spec record settles widening these two props from `string` to `ReactNode`, so a maintainer needs to provide or identify the governing spec for that addition in the `DialogHeader` contract — including the accepted value domain for the required title (plain `ReactNode` also admits empty, boolean, and interactive or block content, while the documented guidance is inline, non-interactive, and non-empty) and for the subtitle, including `0` rendering and empty values rendering nothing.

No code change is being requested for this hold itself. Once a maintainer records that governing claim, the change can be re-reviewed against it on the evidence already here.

This change looks good to approve. It corrects CheckboxIndicator guidance so it matches the shipped component on every point: theme authors are pointed to the canonical `checkbox-indicator` target instead of the deprecated `checkbox` alias; the focus guidance now correctly says the owning control paints its standard ring onto the indicator element, so a replacement's root radius shapes the ring; the replacement-content guidance now describes the shallow `isRenderable` branch, including that elements and containers replace the mark even when their descendants render nothing; the type guidance now correctly says a spread-forwarded `tabIndex` is not stripped; and the `isRenderable` guidance no longer promises DOM output from a shallow check.

Nothing is removed or changed at runtime: the legacy `checkbox` target is still emitted on the same element, its deprecated-for metadata still names the canonical replacement, and existing themes keep working. The added `CheckboxIndicator.spec.md` is explicitly a draft that records shipped behavior only and claims no new authority — the empty-container replacement question is left unsettled rather than decided.

The knowledge, changeset, and sync checks pass, along with the focused Indicator, registry, and theming-target tests and lint on the changed source.

Thanks for the careful endpoint fix and regression coverage. The implementation matches the policy you describe — pointer and End can reach the explicit maximum, and arrow keys visit the adjacent selectable value instead of skipping it — and this review found no concrete code defect in the single or range cases; the focused tests and browser checks for the `step=3` case pass.

Approval is waiting on a maintainer decision, though. Slider's current governing contract covers its anatomy and theming and does not settle whether the explicit maximum should join the selectable set when the step does not divide the range, including the shorter final interval, preferring maximum on a tie, arrow movement from off-grid values, and the range-thumb separation case. A maintainer needs to provide or identify the governing spec for that addition before it can be approved; please do not treat this as a request to rewrite the fix or to author the spec yourself.

Once that policy is settled in favour, the remaining step is normal verification on the merged result. If it is settled the other way, the endpoint behaviour would need to change accordingly.

Thanks — the core fix is right: `RichTextEditor` already reflects `size` and `status`, and declaring `visualProps: ['size', 'status']` on the `rich-text-editor` target makes those axes discoverable to theme authors, with a regression test that pins the declaration to the rendered attributes. Two small fixes are needed before this can land:

- **Remove `.changeset/richtext-theme-target.md`.** `@astryxdesign/richtext` is a private, canary-only package, so a Changeset naming it fails the repository's Changeset check — this is the current CI lint failure ("is private/ignored and cannot be released"). No publishable package changes here, so the file should simply be deleted rather than retargeted.
- **Type the new test's doc import.** Importing `./RichTextEditor.doc.mjs` in `RichTextEditor.test.tsx` breaks the richtext package's typecheck (no declaration file for the module, and an implicitly-`any` callback parameter), because the ambient `*.doc.mjs` declaration lives only in the core package. A richtext-local declaration mirroring core's, or loading the doc the way the core theming guard does, would fix it.

With those two changes, the remaining diff is the correct documentation fix and its test.

This change restores `RichTextView` to its documented behavior, and the review recommends approval.

- The view now renders content rather than an unnamed textbox, so heading, list, and link structure is no longer flattened for assistive technology, and the resolved accessibility entries leave the baseline.
- Its own root styles now compose with a consumer `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` on both the normal root and the error fallback — previously those documented inputs were silently discarded.
- `onParseError` is now reported after commit, once per distinct error, instead of being called during render.

No public API changes and no blocking findings. The regression tests cover each behavior, including rendered-DOM assertions for the style merging.

Thank you for this fix — the reasoning is exactly right: a view is content, not a form field, so removing the widget role (and the widget-only ARIA that depends on it) is the correct restoration rather than adding a name to satisfy the checker. The regression tests, the baseline cleanup for the same rule, and the README and `SYNC:` corrections all look good, and the editor path is untouched.

One change is needed before this can be approved:

- **Delete `.changeset/richtextview-not-a-textbox.md`.** `@astryxdesign/richtext` is a private package, and the guardrail check on this revision fails on it: `check:changesets` reports that the package "is private/ignored and cannot be released" (the `lint` job is red for this reason). Since the package is never released through the changeset flow, the fix needs no changeset.

That is the only correction — the `RichTextView` change itself needs no rework.

This change fixes the playground editor flagging imports that the preview renders fine. It synthesizes editor declarations for the modules the runtime scope already serves — `lucide-react` named exports (including the `*Icon` aliases), the neutral and matcha theme packages and their `/built` subpaths, `next/image`, and the bare `stylex` alias — mounts core declarations at the package root so flat subpaths such as `@astryxdesign/core/BaseProps` resolve, and adds a parity test so the runtime scope and the editor type bundle cannot drift apart again.

The follow-up commit synthesizes the theme declarations instead of reading the theme packages' built files, which the CI docsite-test job never builds; the synthesized exports match what the theme build itself emits (the theme value plus its icon registry, with the same types).

No runtime scope, runner, template, or public API changes. The evidence is convincing: the parity test fails against the previous generator with the expected undeclared modules, both issue snippets produce no more TS2305/TS2307 markers after the change, and a negative control shows genuinely invalid imports still error, so diagnostics are fixed rather than suppressed.

This change restores the overlapping layout for `AvatarGroup` when avatars are wrapped in a `HoverCard` or `Tooltip`, which the Avatar docs already recommend. The overlap no longer depends on each avatar being a direct, non-first child of the group, and the group compensates the first item so it stays inside the group's box.

Verified: wrapped avatars now overlap by the same amount as plain avatars and the row returns to the plain group's width, plain groups keep their previous geometry, and new regression tests cover plain, wrapped, and empty groups. No public API changes.

Two disclosed edge interactions are worth knowing about: setting start padding on the group through `xstyle` replaces the compensation, and an avatar rendered inside hover-card or tooltip content still inherits the group's context. Neither blocks this fix.

Thanks for the grouped update — most of this batch is routine, but it can't land as resolved yet:

- **StyleX ends up on two versions at once.** The catalog and direct ranges move to 0.19.1, but `@stylexjs/unplugin` stays at 0.19.0 and its lockfile entry still depends on `@stylexjs/babel-plugin` 0.19.0, so the lockfile keeps both the 0.19.0 and 0.19.1 StyleX sets. CI on this head shows the result: the CLI strict typecheck and the docsite build fail with "two different types with this name exist" errors on StyleX style types. Please make the whole `@stylexjs/*` family resolve to a single version — holding StyleX at 0.19.0 until unplugin catches up, or forcing one version — and confirm those builds pass.
- **The example apps jump a Next.js major.** The four `apps/example-nextjs*` templates move from Next 15 to Next 16 inside a minor/patch batch, and they aren't built in-repo, so there's no evidence they still work. Please drop that change from the examples here, or split it into its own PR with verification.
- **Two sets of pins drifted apart.** `packages/cli` bumps its exact `@babel/parser`, `@babel/plugin-transform-typescript`, and `recast` pins, but the matching `shadcn@4.19.0>` overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` still hold the old values that file says to keep aligned. Please update the overrides to match, or keep the old CLI pins.

Everything else in the batch looked consistent with the manifests and lockfile.

<!-- codebunny-pub:1 k=6fa9383959028e5b1572f7cae354a445e4d28bd69d76b14175888a746b739b20 -->

Thanks — this fixes the single-line scroll cleanly.

With `maxRows={1}`, one short line no longer scrolls: removing the block padding from the editable and its placeholder stops that padding from consuming the `maxRows` height cap under the border-box reset, and the root's one-line minimum drops by the same 8px so the empty input stays the same height and placeholder position when disabled. The before/after measurements (30px scroll height and an 8px scroll range down to 22px and no scroll range, with the old sizing restored as a mutation check) line up with the code, and the multiline, focus, and file-drop paths are unchanged. The updated changeset now names both the scroll fix and the disabled alignment.

One thing worth being aware of at merge time: the one-line input is now 22px tall instead of 30px at every `maxRows` value, including the default, so composers in height-sensitive layouts will shift by 8px. That change is disclosed in the PR and is inseparable from the fix.

## Review

This is ready to merge. The docs graph gives every doc one derived home and one route, every docs and search read now ends with runnable moves, and links between docs are typed by identity instead of hand-written — while the 0.6 JSON contracts (`docs(topic)` returning the whole topic, `--index`, and the `ReferenceContentBlock` union) are preserved and guarded by tests, including the graph walk that opens every doc, move, and link the CLI ships. The spec-owner approval for the current-record amendments in this PR has now been recorded for this revision, so the hold from the previous review is resolved.

Worth knowing for consumers:

- The two breaking changes are labelled as such, with minor changesets and migration guidance: `astryx docs cli-integrations` is now `astryx docs cli/integrations` with no alias (the old name fails with a suggestion of the new route), and a winning integration template replacement removes the Core entry from the default template list, with explicit `--package @astryxdesign/core` selection still reaching the original.
- Integration authors gain namespace docs and placed guides beside `cli`, template replacement with deterministic precedence and fail-closed invalid claims, and a pack check that refuses a package shipping those features whose declared CLI peer range admits a CLI too old to read them — closing the silent doc loss seen on 0.6.3.
- Reads, the topic list, and search now agree on who holds a docs name, and a topic that answers through `replaces` to a route the CLI's own docs keep gets a doctor diagnostic naming it, in one package or across a chain of replacements.
- `themeTemplate()` is now exported from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`, closing the documented parity gap for `astryx theme template`.
- Doctor's new graph findings warn rather than fail, so projects that passed before keep passing.

The still-open items noted in the PR (text-mode errors not printing the error code, resolved JSON links reading as plain command text, and pack check not itself running the docs checks) are reasonable follow-ups and do not block this change.

<!-- codebunny-pub:1 k=499f156193fb536d0bd770b5beeb1f0ab99b0b1e51e431f6e78b4c31f7b23ae6 -->

Thanks for tracking this down to the translucent surface — the contrast diagnosis and the fix itself hold up.

Unselected labels now use the primary text token, which restores the required 4.5:1 where the secondary token fell short (about 3.7:1 on the reported dark backdrop, versus about 7.6:1 for primary), and the new token-pin test guards the regression.

Approval is pending a design decision, though. The same change removes the dimming that distinguished unselected labels from the selected one — in the default story the unselected labels now render in the selected label's colour, so selection rests on the surface fill and the semibold weight. No current design record settles that hierarchy change, and a designer needs to approve this visible contrast treatment before the PR is ready to land — or direct an alternative that holds 4.5:1 while preserving a dimmed unselected label (for example a different surface or an intermediate token).

One small, non-blocking suggestion while that decision is made: the changeset and comments describe the result as at least 7:1 wherever the page's own text passes, which is broader than what is proved for pages whose text only just passes. Qualifying that phrase to the reported and default backdrops would make the release note exact.

This change fixes a real cascade bug: when a theme adaptation only changed the type scale, the regenerated Heading/Text defaults were emitted after the root theme and silently reset authored component styles — for example, a branded display font family reverting on narrow touch viewports. The fix resolves adaptations against the effective root component map and omits only the generated component leaves that already exist at root, so sizes and leading still adapt through the existing variable wiring while authored pins stay authoritative. The important boundaries are preserved and covered by new Core and CLI regression cases: generated scale tokens still write in rule order, authored rule overrides (including one that restores a root value) still win, and themes without a root scale still receive the missing generated defaults.

Approval is not yet possible, because this pull request also intentionally changes the established spec: the current AST-012 FR4 wording says every produced leaf counts as a write by that rule, and FR6 gives the last matching write the win with no root-path exception. Approval needs a maintainer to update the existing spec for that intentional change — an eligible engineering owner giving spec-owner approval to this pull request's FR4/FR6 amendment on its current head, which is still pending. What must be settled is whether invariant generated type-scale component defaults at exact leaf paths already declared on the effective root components are not writes (with generated tokens and rule-authored leaves remaining writes), and whether a later scale-only rule preserves an earlier authored component leaf only when its exact path exists at root, while the generated leaf still wins when that path is absent.

No code changes are requested for this hold. Once a maintainer settles the spec update, the evidence in this change supports approval as it stands.

This is a clean, well-evidenced bug fix. The ISO week-number computation in `plainDateGetWeekNumber` (used by Calendar's week-number column and the exported `getWeekNumber`) mixed local-time `Date` math with day-count division, so in timezones where DST ends after New Year (Sydney, Auckland, Santiago) a stray hour leaked into the count and rounded whole weeks up in Friday-January-1 years — e.g. April 2021 displayed week 15 for ISO week 14.

What I verified:

- The rewrite anchors the Thursday shift and the January 1 reference to UTC, so no wall-clock offset can leak in; the previous implementation's failure and the new values were both reproduced against an independent ISO reference.
- New regression tests cover the three named zones plus a late-December boundary, and they genuinely exercise the DST mechanism (confirmed the timezone switches take effect in the test runner).
- Full `plainDate` (95 tests) and Calendar (186 tests) suites pass, including under the Sydney timezone; typecheck and lint are clean.
- An 11,562-combination sweep across six timezones and sixteen years matches the ISO reference throughout with the new code.

No action needed — the changeset, tests, and fix are consistent and complete. Nice catch on a subtle one.
